noise_summary: 307 off-topic results filtered from five major noise clusters generated by Taiwan actor search terms matching unrelated entities. (1) 'DPP' matched Indonesia's Dewan Pimpinan Pusat party structures (~35 articles from jawapos.com, antaranews.com, cnnindonesia.com, etc.) and Trinidad & Tobago's Director of Public Prosecutions (~8 articles), Malawi DPP, Zambia DPP, Kenya DPP, and other non-Taiwan DPPs. (2) 'KMT' matched KTM motorcycle brand generating ~22 European emissions-scandal articles (lemonde.fr, 20minutes.fr, desmog.com, rideapart.com, etc.). (3) 'Wellington Koo' matched Wellington, New Zealand (~18 articles from nzherald.co.nz, rnz.co.nz, etc.) and Wellington Phoenix football club. (4) 'NSB' (National Security Bureau search term) matched Sri Lanka National Savings Bank, Indian National Sports Board (~10 articles), Ghana National Signals Bureau corruption trial, Thai Narcotics Suppression Bureau, US National Science Board, and WWII Dutch NSB. (5) 'TPP' matched Indonesian Tambahan Penghasilan Pegawai civil servant pay system (~20 articles from jpnn.com, ur-ban.id, etc.), Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Lebanese in the US (~4 articles), and miscellaneous. Additional off-topic noise: ~50 Vietnamese entertainment and local news articles (kenh14.vn, vnexpress.net, vietgiaitri.com, tienphong.vn, etc.) generated by broad regional queries; ~22 Canadian Broadcasting Corporation (CBC) articles; ~20 non-Taiwan Armed Forces articles (UK, US, Ukraine, Malaysia); ~18 Korean entertainment/sports articles; ~6 Hong Kong astronaut Lai Ka-ying articles (disambiguating from President Lai Ching-te); Samsung/SK Hynix Korea technology articles (~5); and miscellaneous sports (PSG/Arsenal Champions League, Super Rugby, MLB) and human-interest items (~12). One duplicate URL noted: taiwannews.com.tw OCAC article and taipeitimes.com DPP China Affairs article each appeared in both [actor] and [vocab] query sections with identical URLs; counted once each.

stories.headline: China conducts repeated PLA combat-readiness patrols around Taiwan; ROC Armed Forces respond
stories.summary: In the week following the Xi–Trump Beijing summit, China conducted at least two 'joint combat readiness patrols' around Taiwan within a single week, deploying over 100 vessels along the First Island Chain, a carrier group, and dozens of aircraft crossing the median line. Taiwan scrambled jets and warships; NSC Secretary-General Joseph Wu publicly condemned the activity as 'unprovoked' and called China 'the sole source of instability in the Indo-Pacific.' A separate tense standoff occurred near the Pratas Islands.

stories.headline: Taiwan's stock market surpasses India to become world's fifth-largest, powered by TSMC AI rally
stories.summary: Taiwan's total market capitalization reached approximately $4.95 trillion in late May, overtaking India ($4.92 trillion) to rank fifth globally behind the US, China, Japan, and Hong Kong. The surge was driven almost entirely by TSMC, which now accounts for roughly 42% of the TAIEX index and is up approximately 49% year-to-date on AI demand. New financial regulations allowing domestic funds to hold up to 25% of net assets in a single stock were expected to channel billions more into TSMC.

stories.headline: TSMC employee bonus dispute escalates; CEO pledges over 30% payout increase
stories.summary: Rumors that TSMC planned to cut employee performance bonuses by approximately 15% spread on social media group 'TSMC大小事,' sparking internal discontent with some employees threatening Samsung-style strike action. Chairman C.C. Wei cancelled travel plans and held a company-wide meeting on May 27 to address the backlash, pledging that total bonuses would grow more than 30% in 2026 compared to 2025, citing the company's record AI-driven revenues.

stories.headline: KMT chair Cheng Li-wun departs for two-week US visit following controversial Beijing trip
stories.summary: KMT Chairwoman Cheng Li-wun departed for a two-week visit to the United States on June 1, where she was scheduled to meet Republican and Democratic lawmakers, officials, and policy experts. The trip came weeks after her historic meeting with Xi Jinping in Beijing—the first between a sitting KMT chair and the Chinese leader in nearly a decade—which had raised questions in Washington about the party's alignment. An incident involving the Jamestown Foundation's president calling DPP sources 'foolish' after a controversy about Cheng's meeting schedule became a minor political flashpoint.

stories.headline: Computex and Nvidia's $150 billion annual Taiwan investment pledge spotlight island's AI centrality
stories.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang arrived in Taiwan ahead of Computex, declaring Taiwan the 'epicentre' of the AI revolution and pledging up to $150 billion per year in Taiwan investment. AMD also announced $10 billion-plus AI sector investment. Taiwan's government statistics agency separately raised its 2026 GDP growth forecast to a 16-year high, attributing the upward revision to AI-related demand led by TSMC. Jensen Huang met with TSMC Chairman C.C. Wei and hosted a large supplier banquet.

stories.headline: MediaTek shareholder meeting reaffirms TSMC partnership while adopting Intel advanced packaging as alternative
stories.summary: At its May 29 shareholder meeting, MediaTek CEO Rick Tsai confirmed TSMC remains the company's 'most important and long-term' foundry partner across all nodes, dismissing speculation that Samsung might displace it. Separately, MediaTek announced it now supports both TSMC's CoWoS and Intel's EMIB advanced packaging technologies, giving customers choice and doubling its 2026 data center revenue forecast to $2 billion. MediaTek also flagged possible price hikes amid rising memory costs.

stories.headline: China expels New York Times reporter over Lai interview; Taiwan condemns act and vows not to be silenced
stories.summary: China expelled New York Times reporter Vivian Wang from Beijing in February—a decision revealed publicly in late May—after the paper published an interview with President Lai Ching-te at the DealBook Summit. Taiwan's presidential office condemned the expulsion as 'groundless,' saying it was standard practice for Lai to give interviews. The US separately revoked the visa of a Xinhua journalist in apparent retaliation, deepening a US-China media standoff and raising concerns among Western outlets about covering Taiwan.

stories.headline: Possible Trump-Lai phone call on arms deal discussed; Taiwan urges stronger US ties amid uncertainty
stories.summary: President Trump indicated he might speak directly with President Lai about a pending arms sales package reportedly worth up to $8 billion, a move that would break with diplomatic protocol. Lai gifted Trump a two-volume autobiography of TSMC founder Morris Chang as a diplomatic gesture. US Defense Secretary Hegseth sidestepped Taiwan arms questions at the Shangri-La Dialogue, with analysts warning that ambiguity could signal Taiwan is 'tradable.' KMT's Taichung Mayor Lu Shiow-yen separately called on Lai to proactively pursue the call.

stories.headline: KMT pursues domestic legislative agenda: flogging referendum, acting official limits, and e-sports law
stories.summary: KMT lawmakers advanced a referendum proposal to introduce corporal punishment for certain serious crimes, pending Legislative Yuan review. Separately, a KMT lawmaker proposed a six-month cap on acting appointments to government agency leadership positions to protect legislative ratification rights. KMT legislators also called on the government to pass a basic act governing e-sports development, arguing current policy lacks the legislative backbone to support Taiwan's competitive hardware advantages.

stories.summary: A five-member cross-party German parliamentary delegation visiting Taiwan through May 31 met with President Lai Ching-te and other senior officials including NSC Secretary-General Joseph Wu. Taiwan cited TSMC's semiconductor facility in Dresden as an important milestone in bilateral technology cooperation, and DPP lawmakers asserted that Taiwan-Germany ties are not subject to PRC approval.

stories.headline: TSMC plans to raise 3nm process pricing up to 15% in second half of 2026
stories.summary: Reports emerged that TSMC plans to raise prices for its 3-nanometer advanced process nodes by up to 15% in the second half of 2026, with a further 5-10% increase possible in 2027. The move reflects surging demand from Nvidia, Google, and AWS that exceeds TSMC's capacity expansion pace. TSMC Chairman C.C. Wei was expected to address pricing and AI demand at the company's June 4 shareholder meeting.

stories.summary: The Trump administration moved to remove certain tariffs on Taiwan imports—specifically derivative aluminum, steel, and copper duties on aircraft components—to implement parts of a previously agreed trade deal between Washington and Taipei. The move was framed as formalizing an earlier Memorandum of Understanding on investment.
